memory_candidates.topic: Transporting a step-path classification to a splice classification in BimodalLogic
memory_candidates.insight: WorldHistory.path is WorldHistory.state by definition and seamOmegaEquiv's .symm carries the seam condition as its .2 field, so a classification of bare step paths through a seam state applies to `spliced tau t bf`.path directly -- no pathFibreEquiv rewrite is needed, and WorldHistory.ext_state lifts the pointwise result to a history equality. A plan predicting this transport as the cost driver of a phase mispredicted: it is ~29 lines.

memory_candidates.topic: Scope estimation for per-letter closure-alphabet read-outs
memory_candidates.insight: A plan item of the form 'for each member of the closure plus the marker, give the trace on each of N families explicitly' multiplies out: a 4-member closure and 2 families is 10 per-letter lemmas, and the supporting exhaustion lemma, membership facts, falsity lemmas and assembled forms bring it to ~21 declarations. Estimating such an item at 80-120 lines undershoots by roughly a factor of two; count the declarations the item implies before writing the hypothesis.

memory_candidates.topic: Avoiding pairwise-distinctness lemmas in a letter-indexed iff read-out
memory_candidates.insight: When proving `trace q z <-> (q = letter1 /\ P1 z) \/ (q = letter2 /\ P2 z) \/ ...`, prove the forward direction by case-splitting on an alphabet-exhaustion lemma and the backward direction by `rintro (<rfl, h> | rfl | ...)`. The rfl patterns substitute the letter variable, so no letter needs to be distinguished from any other and the pairwise-distinctness lemmas are never consulted -- which also keeps the proof free of simp-argument-list churn and its unusedSimpArgs warnings.
